searchText: > Contract pays gas. Contract wallet that doesn't require signer have gas money. ✅ Base EIP-2938 supports this. > Sponsored Transactions. Totally unrelated address pays for gas than is CALLER. CALLER can be a contract wallet ✅ EIP-3074 handles this and works with AA > Multi-action transactions. Example: Approve then Call atomically, both with msg.sender of owner. ✅ Base EIP-2938 supports this. > EOA == Contract. isHuman and isContract should not be possible. Contracts should not be able to discriminate against people securing their assets smartly! ❌ `EXTCODESIZE` makes this impossible without some sweeping changes. > Arbitrary Executions. A contract wallet should be able to do arbitrary things, not only what it was programmed to do (e.g., caller passes an array of contracts and calldatas to call in order). ✅ Base EIP-2938 supports this > Third Party Callers. A contract wallet should be able to receive incoming calls from other contracts. ✅ Supported with `COMMIT_GAS`: https://hackmd.io/@SamWilsn/S1UQDOzBv#Read-write-Calls > Account Storage. A contract wallet should be able to store data, and that data should be publicly visible.(edited) ✅ Supported with base EIP-2938 Accessing your own state is always allowed before `PAYGAS`, and the contract can choose what limits to apply, just like a regular contract. If all EOAs were converted to AA accounts, wouldn't that break extcodesize? Yep, though you could do an `EXTCODECOPY` and check it against some whitelist. I feel like as long as contracts can discriminate on human vs contract caller, they will discriminate. And as long as contracts discriminate on that, people will not switch to using contract accounts. It is one of my fears with going down the AA path rather than something like rich transactions. How often is `EXTCODECOPY` even used? For anything other than isHuman checks? Yeah My guess is never, but I can't prove it. Oh, it is used by bots for gas savings. Using a contract as a constant? It is cheaper to write contracts when storing large amounts of data. lol! There are good reasons though, and it isn't an exploit, even if it is dumb. Contracts are contiguous storage, while every 32 bytes in storage is a merkle node. _Very_ expensive writes, and cheap reads Or something along those lines. Ah, is it expensive to write, cheap to read? Yep Makes sense You'd need to do a self-destruct then deploy to write I'm not too worried about those people. But `EXTCODECOPY` to read. Maybe an EIP to remove them, or make them always return a zero length? I support pretty much all extreme measures to stop the isContract behavior. That's about the only way to actually make isHuman checks impossible to implement. My concern is that if we implement AA without those extreme measures we may not reap the benefits of AA. Ah, well... `tx.origin` will always be `ENTRY_POINT` I think? However, I also worry we won't be able to convince the core devs to implement extreme measures. I'll have to check the EIP to be sure. I would rather tx.origin be the AA account, for basically the same reason. > If ORIGIN (0x32) is invoked in any frame of execution of an AA transaction it must return AA_ENTRY_POINT. Yeah, I don't like that because it provides a discriminant. `require(tx.origin == msg.sender)` Yep I think it should return the target contract as well.

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content:
> Contract pays gas.  Contract wallet that doesn't require signer have gas money.

✅  Base EIP-2938 supports this.

> Sponsored Transactions.  Totally unrelated address pays for gas than is CALLER.  CALLER can be a contract wallet

✅  EIP-3074 handles this and works with AA

> Multi-action transactions.  Example: Approve then Call atomically, both with msg.sender of owner.

✅  Base EIP-2938 supports this.

> EOA == Contract.  isHuman and isContract should not be possible.  Contracts should not be able to discriminate against people securing their assets smartly!

❌ `EXTCODESIZE` makes this impossible without some sweeping changes.

> Arbitrary Executions.  A contract wallet should be able to do arbitrary things, not only what it was programmed to do (e.g., caller passes an array of contracts and calldatas to call in order).

✅  Base EIP-2938 supports this

> Third Party Callers. A contract wallet should be able to receive incoming calls from other contracts.

✅  Supported with `COMMIT_GAS`: https://hackmd.io/@SamWilsn/S1UQDOzBv#Read-write-Calls

> Account Storage. A contract wallet should be able to store data, and that data should be publicly visible.(edited)

✅  Supported with base EIP-2938
